title: Shoreditch Emergency Help Points
summary: Emergency medical facilities, walk-in centres, hazards, and essential supplies in Shoreditch.
content:
For life-threatening emergencies, call 999 or 112 immediately.

1. 24-Hour Emergency Hospitals (A&E):
- The Royal London Hospital (Major Trauma Centre): Whitechapel Road, E1 1FR. From Shoreditch High Street station: ~20 min walk south along Commercial Street and east along Whitechapel Road (approx 1 mile), or bus 205 eastbound.
- Moorfields Eye Hospital (Eye Emergencies Only, 24/7): 162 City Road, EC1V 2PD. From Old Street station: ~3 min walk north along City Road.
- Homerton University Hospital: Homerton Row, E9 6SR. From Shoreditch High Street: bus 242 eastbound towards Homerton.

2. Urgent Treatment Centres:
- The Royal London Urgent Treatment Centre: Ground Floor, Stepney Way / Whitechapel Road, E1 1FR. Walk-in access via main A&E entrance.
- City and Hackney Urgent Treatment Centre: Located inside Homerton University Hospital, Homerton Row, E9 6SR.

3. Local Hazards & Infrastructure:
- High pedestrian density around Shoreditch High Street, Old Street roundabout, and Great Eastern Street can create severe bottlenecks during mass transits or evacuations.
- Regent's Canal corridor to the north carries minor localized surface water flood risks during severe weather events.

4. Supplies & Essentials:
- Supermarkets and pharmacies along Shoreditch High Street, Great Eastern Street, and Old Street stock essential batteries, water, first-aid items, and medication.

Note: addresses and opening hours may have changed — confirm on arrival where possible (verify locally).
